message.content: {"answer": "B", "option_text": "Unilateral diaphragmatic paralysis on the right side", "reason": "Visual inspection confirms significant elevation of the right hemidiaphragm with a smooth, intact contour and no meniscus sign or blunting of the costophrenic angle, effectively ruling out pleural effusion (A). The absence of bowel loops in the chest excludes congenital hernia (C), and the lack of hyperinflation/flattening rules out COPD (E). While hepatomegaly (F) can elevate the diaphragm, the specific combination of marked unilateral elevation without an underlying mass effect or fluid is the classic radiographic presentation of unilateral diaphragmatic paralysis. The report generator's mention of 'mild pulmonary edema' does not explain the focal structural asymmetry, necessitating reliance on direct pixel evidence per skill t000006."}
